units.text: INT. HUSBAND - CONTINUOUS
Robert, it is not true, is it? You are not going to lend your support to this Argentine speculation? You couldn’t!
units.name: LADY CHILTERN

units.text: Starting .
Who told you I intended to do so?
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: That woman who has just gone out, Mrs. Cheveley, as she calls herself now. She seemed to taunt me with it. Robert, I know this woman. You don’t. We were at school together. She was untruthful, dishonest, an evil influence on every one whose trust or friendship she could win. I hated, I despised her. She stole things, she was a thief. She was sent away for being a thief. Why do you let her influence you?
units.name: LADY CHILTERN

units.text: Gertrude, what you tell me may be true, but it happened many years ago. It is best forgotten! Mrs. Cheveley may have changed since then. No one should be entirely judged by their past.
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: Sadly .
One’s past is what one is. It is the only way by which people should be judged.
units.name: LADY CHILTERN

units.text: That is a hard saying, Gertrude!
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: It is a true saying, Robert. And what did she mean by boasting that she had got you to lend your support, your name, to a thing I have heard you describe as the most dishonest and fraudulent scheme there has ever been in political life?
units.name: LADY CHILTERN

units.text: Biting his lip .
I was mistaken in the view I took. We all may make mistakes.
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: But you told me yesterday that you had received the report from the Commission, and that it entirely condemned the whole thing.
units.name: LADY CHILTERN

units.text: Walking up and down .

I have reasons now to believe that the Commission was prejudiced, or, at any rate, misinformed. Besides, Gertrude, public and private life are different things. They have different laws, and move on different lines.
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: They should both represent man at his highest. I see no difference between them.
units.name: LADY CHILTERN

units.text: Stopping .
In the present case, on a matter of practical politics, I have changed my mind. That is all.
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: All!
units.name: LADY CHILTERN

units.text: Sternly .
Yes!
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: Robert! Oh! it is horrible that I should have to ask you such a question—Robert, are you telling me the whole truth?
units.name: LADY CHILTERN

units.text: Why do you ask me such a question?
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: After a pause .
Why do you not answer it?
units.name: LADY CHILTERN

units.text: Sitting down .

Gertrude, truth is a very complex thing, and politics is a very complex business. There are wheels within wheels. One may be under certain obligations to people that one must pay. Sooner or later in political life one has to compromise. Every one does.
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: Compromise? Robert, why do you talk so differently to-night from the way I have always heard you talk? Why are you changed?
units.name: LADY CHILTERN

units.text: I am not changed. But circumstances alter things.
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: Circumstances should never alter principles!
units.name: LADY CHILTERN

units.text: But if I told you—
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: What?
units.name: LADY CHILTERN

units.text: That it was necessary, vitally necessary?
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: It can never be necessary to do what is not honourable. Or if it be necessary, then what is it that I have loved! But it is not, Robert; tell me it is not. Why should it be? What gain would you get? Money? We have no need of that! And money that comes from a tainted source is a degradation. Power? But power is nothing in itself. It is power to do good that is fine—that, and that only. What is it, then? Robert, tell me why you are going to do this dishonourable thing!
units.name: LADY CHILTERN

units.text: Gertrude, you have no right to use that word. I told you it was a question of rational compromise. It is no more than that.
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: Robert, that is all very well for other men, for men who treat life simply as a sordid speculation; but not for you, Robert, not for you. You are different. All your life you have stood apart from others. You have never let the world soil you. To the world, as to myself, you have been an ideal always. Oh! be that ideal still. That great inheritance throw not away—that tower of ivory do not destroy. Robert, men can love what is beneath them—things unworthy, stained, dishonoured. We women worship when we love; and when we lose our worship, we lose everything. Oh! don’t kill my love for you, don’t kill that!
units.name: LADY CHILTERN

units.text: Gertrude!
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: I know that there are men with horrible secrets in their lives—men who have done some shameful thing, and who in some critical moment have to pay for it, by doing some other act of shame—oh! don’t tell me you are such as they are! Robert, is there in your life any secret dishonour or disgrace? Tell me, tell me at once, that—
units.name: LADY CHILTERN

units.text: That what?
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: Speaking very slowly .
That our lives may drift apart.
units.name: LADY CHILTERN

units.text: Drift apart?
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: That they may be entirely separate. It would be better for us both.
units.name: LADY CHILTERN

units.text: Gertrude, there is nothing in my past life that you might not know.
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: I was sure of it, Robert, I was sure of it. But why did you say those dreadful things, things so unlike your real self? Don’t let us ever talk about the subject again. You will write, won’t you, to Mrs. Cheveley, and tell her that you cannot support this scandalous scheme of hers? If you have given her any promise you must take it back, that is all!
units.name: LADY CHILTERN

units.text: Must I write and tell her that?
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN
